adversarialReview.objection: Deleting the mapping deletes its TOTALITY guard (module doc: an unrecognised value yields null rather than being passed through). After the change an out-of-grammar DB value would reach the wire raw.
adversarialReview.assessment: Accepted as a real property loss, judged acceptable, surviving control named.
adversarialReview.survivingControl: lib/db/drizzle/0092_pe_billing_interval.sql:49-52 CONSTRAINT pe_user_entitlements_billing_interval_chk -- billing_interval IS NULL OR billing_interval IN ('month','year'). A DDL CHECK binds every writer including raw connections, which a TypeScript union never does. ENFORCEMENT: where a type can express the constraint, prefer the type over any check.
adversarialReview.residualRisk: drizzle .$type<PeBillingInterval>() is an UNCHECKED cast, so TypeScript is not the runtime guarantee here; the CHECK constraint is. The column was ADDed and CHECKed in the same migration (0092), so there is no pre-constraint legacy population holding an out-of-grammar value.
adversarialReview.provenanceOfSnapValue: snap.billingInterval has exactly two origins: peIdentity.ts:181 (row?.billingInterval ?? null, read from the constrained column) and peEntitlement.ts:111 (hardcoded null for the unauthenticated snapshot). Neither can produce a third string.
